National Assembly
Bishau Adhiveshan
Complete Details of Proceedings
March 22, 2082
Sunday
Meeting Number -
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 12:22 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly commence at (12:22 PM). Honourable Members, I will provide time to the Honourable Members who have been listed to speak during the Zero Hour. I have allocated 1 minute of time to each member for speaking in the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Uday Bahadur Bohora.

Honourable Mr. Uday Bahadur Bohora (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, due to the war between America, Israel, and Iran in South Asia, specifically in the Gulf countries, 80 to 84 thousand Nepalis are in an unsafe situation. There are reports of one death and some injuries due to violence. A large number of Nepalis wish to return to their homeland; their safety needs to be ensured, and arrangements should be made for those wishing to return safely. I wish to draw the attention of the government through the Honourable Chairperson. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Parki.

Honourable Mr. Jagat Bahadur Parki (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, in Ward No. 7 of Alital Rural Municipality, Dadeldhura district, from August 19 to September 30, 2077 BS, 46 families were displaced in a village called Balaucha. Even after 5 years, they have not been resettled. A government team, after a geological survey team visited, recommended their resettlement, but it has not happened yet. Therefore, through the Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw the serious attention of the Government of Nepal to their timely resettlement. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.

Honourable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):- Honourable Chairperson, it has been almost three months, and we are all experiencing it. There is an extreme shortage of gas. This problem is not only here but in many countries worldwide. However, alternatives like electric gas, electric stoves, or induction stoves are only suitable for small families. For large families with children, it is a significant problem. Waiting in line for 14 days, not getting it, and having to buy other things as well – consumers are currently facing such treatment. I wish to draw the serious attention of the current government to this, and I want the government to provide services to the public after they pay. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.

Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, the Martyr Dashrath Chand Medical University is located in Geta, Kailali district, in Sudurpashchim. The impressive sight of numerous buildings resembling a small town constructed in the name of Geta Medical College is visible. These buildings have now become the property of the university. Whether a university requires more than just a name remains to be seen, and the government's attention will surely be drawn to that. The aspiration of the people there is for the 600-bed hospital and MBBS studies to commence as soon as possible. It seems this government is also stirring, but we can have faith in future actions. I believe that this government, rather than just making promises like previous governments, will definitely commence MBBS studies and arrange for a 600-bed hospital from this academic session. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.

Honourable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, in the murder case of Birendra BK of Ward No. 1, Birendranagar Municipality, Surkhet, the police and government lawyers have submitted a report that could lead to the acquittal of the perpetrator. Why is the state so cruel to the Dalit community? Why are there conspiracies and schemes? Will the oppressed Dalit community never get justice?

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".

Honourable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):- Honourable Chairperson, there is a feeder road to the Hulaki Highway from Lamki to Khakraula in Kailali. Under this, a 6-lane road has been constructed from Jamara Bridge to Buspark in Tikapur Municipality-1. Its base is very good, strong, and robust, but due to the extremely weak blacktopping, it has started to break down. Through the Honourable Chairperson, I wish to request the government to asphalt the approximately 2.5-kilometer road. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Mohammad Khalid.

Honourable Mr. Mohammad Khalid (Janata Samajwadi Party Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, the war between America, Israel, and Iran is escalating. We are learning about the damages being incurred by the warring parties through social media. However, the impact of this war is being felt worldwide, especially in South Asia. Due to the abnormal increase in oil prices, every individual in Nepal is also starting to be affected. Therefore, I wish to draw the government's attention to diplomatic efforts for the end of this war and for controlling inflation.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.

Honourable Ms. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepali Communist Party):- Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw attention to an incident in Palpa district. Fourteen-year-old Kishore Neupane has been missing from Palpa since August 22, 2068 BS, which is almost 14 years now. His father has been approaching successive governments and presenting his case. He has not been found yet. I wish to draw the attention of the government and the assembly to search for him for the sake of the family. Also, inflation has increased significantly, and attention has not been paid to it. It is difficult to make a living. I wish to draw the government's attention. Incidents involving women and girls are happening day by day; we cannot bear this pain. I wish to draw attention to minimizing this. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.

Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):- Honourable Chairperson, yesterday I read in the media that this government has banned student organizations affiliated with various political parties. In a political multi-party system, various parties are formed based on political ideology. Various organizations can also be affiliated with these parties. This is a completely democratic matter, a democratic practice. It is not illegal, unconstitutional, or objectionable. Therefore, the ban imposed by this government on student organizations must be lifted. If this government is democratic, does this decision by the government indicate the return of the autocratic Panchayat system, which the Nepali people cremated 36 years ago? Is it a repetition of that system? I don't think so; I believe this government is democratic. If that is the case, the Government of Nepal should immediately revoke and withdraw this decision to ban student organizations. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa.

Honourable Mr. Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, the price of petroleum in the Middle East has increased. Similarly, the price of aviation fuel has increased, inflation has risen, and airfares have increased, imposing a significant financial burden on the general public and greatly affecting their livelihoods. Gas supply is also not smooth. In such a situation, I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to take appropriate steps, keeping this in mind. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the "Zero Hour" for Honourable Members to speak concludes here. Honourable Members, the names of newly elected Honourable Members have been presented to speak. Now, I will provide time to the Honourable Members sequentially. I have allocated 5 minutes of time to each Honourable Member to speak. First, Honourable Member Khamm Bahadur Khalti.

Honourable Mr. Khamm Bahadur Khalti (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, Honourable Members, I would like to express my respect and gratitude to the voters who have represented us in the National Assembly by casting their valuable votes for the representatives, village chairs, vice-chairs, mayors, deputy mayors, and provincial assembly members. I wish to pay homage to all the martyrs who lost their lives and sacrificed themselves in various past political movements. It is necessary to make the federal democratic republic successful and effective. For this, commitment to pluralism, political stability, and trust among parties, and dispelling the despair of the general public are equally essential. It is also equally necessary to amend and revise the Constitution of Nepal and existing laws and regulations to reflect the time, circumstances, and events. Politics is a means of serving the people, not just a tool for acquiring power. In today's political context, there is a drought of political culture, ethics, and responsibility. This weakens democracy and public trust, so we need to be vigilant about it. We need to place special emphasis on political stability and policy continuity. It is necessary to make the implementation of federalism effective. Special emphasis needs to be placed on good governance, transparency, and corruption control. Youth employment and economic development need to be prioritized. It is necessary for the executive, legislature, and judiciary to coordinate and cooperate rather than interfere with each other. If we can all rise above party interests and engage in politics with national interests and public concerns at the center, the country can achieve stability, development, and prosperity. I express my belief and commitment to this. Finally, I congratulate the cabinet of the independent party, which came close to a two-thirds majority, led by Balendra Shah, and wish them a successful tenure. I also request the Government of Nepal to move forward by protecting constitutionalism, the rule of law, human rights, and freedom. Now, in this National Assembly, in the absence of the esteemed members of the parliament, our role is at the forefront from both a challenging and opportunistic perspective. We need to establish a system, and that system is the necessity and relevance of constitutionalism, the rule of law, and our strong determination. We can only move forward with that. The National Assembly is the only assembly where the intellectual circle is represented, and intellectuals, keeping the country and the people at the center, carry out our work. The most important aspect is coordination and cooperation. As we represent in the National Assembly and move around in the press, an unusual and detailed...

There is a local government, a provincial government, and a federal government. We are seeing a lack of coordination between the local government and the provincial government, as well as the federal government. In the coming days, when we amend laws and existing legislation, based on my own experience, the deputy mayor and mayor, and even more so the deputy mayor, have a primary role in planning. While estimating costs, they often sign without fully understanding, leading to many financial cases being handled by the authorities. Therefore, as we move forward with coordination and cooperation, by sitting together, paying special attention to traditional policies and practices, and by supporting and cooperating with the constructive work of the upcoming government, I will bid farewell from here with a commitment to oppose any wrongdoings. I would like to thank the Right Honourable Chairperson and all Honourable Members for providing this opportunity again. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
(12:38 PM)

Honourable Ms. Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, I am happy and proud to be able to address the National Assembly for the first time since being elected.
(12:39 PM)
I would like to pay my respects and tributes to all the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the democratic movement at this important moment. I congratulate all the Honourable Members who were victorious in the National Assembly elections held on January 11th. I extend my heartfelt thanks to all the provincial assembly members and the mayors and deputy mayors who elected me from Bagmati Province in this election, and I express my deep gratitude to my party, the Nepali Congress, for entrusting me with this responsibility. I also congratulate all the Members of Parliament elected in the House of Representatives election held on February 21st and all the members of the newly formed Council of Ministers, and wish them a successful tenure.

Honourable Chairperson, the National Assembly has its own value and importance in Nepal's parliamentary practice. The legitimacy of this institution, which is responsible for providing national guardianship, is proven by the role and conduct of all of us members. For some time now, negative messages have been circulating on social media and in the media regarding the presence, role, and relevance of the National Assembly. In such a situation, all of us MPs must rise above party politics and strengthen the role of the National Assembly as a centre of national unity, trust, and confidence through our good deeds, protecting the overall national interest and the constitution, and amplifying the voices of the people.
Politics is a cyclical game. I hope this meeting inspires everyone to fulfill the responsibilities given by the people through mutual understanding, coordination, and cooperation at this important juncture of nation-building, without being afflicted by the arrogance of the majority or the inferiority complex of the minority.

Honourable Chairperson, there are many challenges facing the country today. The increasing emigration of youth, declining interest in agriculture, rising unemployment, and basic problems connected to the daily lives of the people. These are not just statistics; they are the pains of our society. I particularly want to raise the issue of the agricultural sector. In an agricultural country like Nepal, farmers are still insecure. Production happens, but there is no guarantee of a market. Prices are not fixed, and costs are increasing. In this situation, it is extremely necessary for the state to ensure everything from production to market, implement farmer-friendly policies, technology, and subsidies effectively. In this situation, it is extremely necessary for the state to ensure everything from production to market, implement farmer-friendly policies, technology, and subsidies effectively.

Honourable Chairperson, another serious issue today is youth migration. Our country's capable and energetic youth are forced to go abroad. If this situation continues, the future of the country will be weakened. We must bring policies focused on creating employment, entrepreneurship, and progressive development within the country.

Honourable Chairperson, I would also like to add the issue of women's empowerment here. If women are given opportunities, they can change the country. However, women's participation in decision-making processes is still limited. Equal opportunities, access to leadership, and economic self-reliance must be ensured.

Finally, rather than pursuing impossible dreams, we must prioritize the national interest, the expectations of the people, and the responsibility for the future, rising above politics. Honourable Chairperson, I make a commitment here. I will always raise my voice for the people, for truth, and for the national interest. Thank you, Jai Nepal.

Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Chandra Bahadur KC.
(12:43 PM)

Honourable Mr. Chandra Bahadur KC (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, all Honourable Members, Jai Nepal. I would like to pay my heartfelt tribute to all the known and unknown martyrs.
(12:43 PM)
I express my gratitude and thanks to all the MPs and the village municipality chairpersons, vice-chairpersons, mayors, and deputy mayors who brought me to the National Assembly.

The country seems to be moving forward embracing a new situation and a new era. What is the time, where is the situation, and what are our responsibilities? All political parties in Nepal are currently seeking answers to these questions. In parliamentary practice, the concept of 'majority in power, opposition in opposition' was highlighted by the late Speaker Daman Nath Dhungana and followed up by Subash Nembang. I am not sure how much the subsequent Speakers have embraced it. However, I want this to be kept in mind. In this regard, I am reminded of a philosopher's saying: 'Dissent is the mother of democracy.' If we cannot embrace dissent, democracy cannot flourish. Democracy cannot be strong, it cannot be invincible, it cannot be cut and dried, it cannot be exact.
Therefore, the responsibility to nurture it lies with the Rastriya Swatantra Party, which has reached a historic turning point in Nepal's history, securing 182 seats. I wish them well in moving forward with a great sense of responsibility and accountability. However, if one rides a fast horse, not only the horse but also the rider can fall. Let this be kept in mind. Along with this, I also want to say that since I am new and have spoken a lot, I will learn a lot from the Honourable Members who have been here for a long time, and then we will present and raise new issues. There are things to learn.

In the current context of Nepal, we believe that the current government, the majority government led by Balen, will provide 'lots of pictures.' However, if those pictures do not become actual pictures but only frameworks, then those frameworks will be meaningless. In that sense, I hope this government moves forward. In another sense, many political, economic, and social aspects of Nepal are in disarray. It is the responsibility of the current majority government, which is close to a two-thirds majority, to bring them back on track. If we look at history and consider past events, the Congress government had a two-thirds majority in 2015. Considering the internal and external pressures and events of that time, let us not allow the political dynamics of global power centres to disrupt the lives of the Nepali people due to a two-thirds majority government. I wish for that.

Furthermore, there are many challenges and problems before us. The National Assembly possesses the strength to face them, the capacity to resolve them, and the power to carry them forward together in unity and reconciliation. It has its own significance at the international and national levels. I hope the majority government understands this significance. I hope it can participate in the journey of elevating the dignity of the National Assembly to higher and highest points.

Recently, there have been discussions about constitutional amendments in Nepal. There are also talks of looking at the constitution through the lens of amendment. What is the eye, what is the perspective for looking at amendments? I don't think all these things can be done haphazardly. For that, the unity and reconciliation of Nepal's existing political parties are essential. Inter-party relations will only strengthen and advance it. Therefore, if anyone tries to undermine the dignity of this National Assembly, to belittle its importance, or to lower its significance, it will not yield good results. There is an English saying: 'It is better to love than lost never to love at all.' I hope this significance will be understood, and with that, I conclude my remarks. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Members, the turn of the newly elected Honourable Members to speak will continue in the next meeting, and I wish to inform you of this. Honourable Members, in accordance with Rule 149, Sub-rule (1) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I have nominated and transferred Honourable Members to the thematic committees of the National Assembly as follows:

Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha, Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota, Honourable Member Jagat Timilsina, Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire, and Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur have been nominated to the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee.

Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri, Honourable Member Prem Prasad Dengal, Honourable Member Kham Bahadur Khatri, and Honourable Member Gita Devkota have been nominated to the Legislation Management Committee.

Honourable Member Somnath Poudel, Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhal, Honourable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa, Honourable Member Chandra Bahadur KC, and Honourable Member Ranjit Karna have been nominated to the State Affairs and Public Policy Committee.

Honourable Member Lila Kumari Bhandari, Honourable Member Roshni Mechhe, Honourable Member Lalit Jung Shahi, and Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan have been nominated to the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee.

Honourable Member Mohammad Khalid has been transferred from the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee to the Legislation Management Committee. Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma has been transferred from the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee to the Legislation Management Committee. Honourable Rajendra Laxmi Gaire has been transferred from the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee to the Legislation Management Committee. Honourable Member Renu Chand has been transferred from the State Affairs and Public Policy Committee to the Legislation Management Committee.

2. Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary has been transferred from the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee to the State Affairs and Public Policy Committee. Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Parki has been transferred from the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee to the State Affairs and Public Policy Committee.

3. Honourable Member Srikrishna Prasad Adhikari has been transferred from the State Affairs and Public Policy Committee to the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee. Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai has been transferred from the Legislation Management Committee to the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee.

Honourable Members, the nomination and transfer of Honourable Members to the thematic committees...

I request you to provide your consent to the meeting. Honorable members, I inform you that the nomination and transfer of honorable members for the thematic committee has been consented to by the assembly. Honorable members, in accordance with Rule 10, Sub-rule (1) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I have nominated the following honorable members to chair the meeting in the absence of the chairperson and deputy chairperson. Honorable member Puja Chaudhary, Honorable member Renu Chand, Honorable member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini, and Honorable member Samjhana Devkota. I request you to provide your consent to these members. Honorable members, I declare that the proposed honorable members have received consent from the assembly. Honorable members, now, on behalf of the Right Honorable Prime Minister, I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, to present the "Annual Report of the National Women Commission for the Fiscal Year 2080/081." Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam: Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the Annual Report of the National Women Commission for the Fiscal Year 2081/082 to this esteemed assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Monday, Chaitra 23, 2082, at 12:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned. (Thereafter, the next meeting will be held on Monday, Chaitra 23, 2082, at 12:15 PM, and this meeting was adjourned.) Adjourned: 12:44 PM.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting commenced at 12:22 PM under the chairmanship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The Chairperson announced the commencement of the proceedings and the allocation of time for the Zero Hour.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening of the session and Zero Hour procedures

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: During the Zero Hour, members raised concerns about the safety of Nepalis in the Gulf due to the Iran-US conflict, the resettlement of displaced families in Dadeldhura, the gas shortage and its impact, the establishment of a medical university in Geta, the murder case of Birendra BK, the poor quality of road construction in Kailali, the impact of the Iran-US war on prices, the disappearance of a teenager in Palpa, rising inflation, increasing incidents against women, and the government's ban on student organizations. Members urged the government to address these issues.

sections.summary_en: Following the Zero Hour, the Chairperson announced the conclusion of the Zero Hour and proceeded to the next agenda item, which involved providing time to newly elected members. Honourable Member Khamm Bahadur Khalti delivered a speech.

sections.summary_en: A member discusses the lack of coordination between local, provincial, and federal governments, highlighting issues in planning and cost estimation at the local level. Another member expresses pride in addressing the National Assembly for the first time, pays tribute to martyrs, congratulates newly elected members, and emphasizes the importance of the National Assembly in national unity and constitutional defense. A third member reflects on the nature of parliamentary democracy, the responsibilities of the ruling party, and the challenges facing the nation, including youth migration, agriculture, and women's empowerment.

The Chairperson then proceeds to inform the assembly about the nomination and transfer of members to various thematic committees, including the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Legislation Management Committee, State Affairs and Public Policy Committee, and Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee.
